attack_mechanism: `openMSP430.frontend_0.exec_dext_rdy` sets the selected completion class, execution state, or transition into the required terminal state; the state and data choices on this path depend on `openMSP430.frontend_0.exec_jmp`. The hardware dependence follows `openMSP430.frontend_0.exec_dext_rdy -> openMSP430.frontend_0.e_state_nxt -> openMSP430.frontend_0.e_state -> openMSP430.frontend_0.exec_done`. For a ordinary execution instruction, `exec_done` is produced by the default `(e_state == E_EXEC)` completion arm. An attacker who forces `openMSP430.frontend_0.exec_dext_rdy` away from its terminal value can keep the selected predicate false on successive `mclk` cycles. Decode and fetch remain blocked waiting for completion, creating a persistent loss of instruction retirement.
